marks.gloss_en: 'holy people' (Deut 14:21) / 'holy men ... tereifa ... cast it to the dogs' (Ex 22:30): as there forbidden to eat and permitted for benefit, so here
'ha-zera' -- forbidden on rooting
'ha-melea'a' -- forbidden only if it grew
Abaye: sown [in the vineyard] from the outset -- [forbidden] at rooting

אלא, Rav Mordechai in Reish Lakish's name: one-from-two even by anything; one-from-three, if the argument reverts and comes by מה הצד, by anything, and if not, only by leniency and stringency (= p_rm_chada_mitartei, p_rm_chada_mitelat)
Rav Mordechai (אלא) in Reish Lakish's name: one-from-one we refute by leniency and stringency, not by anything; one-from-two we refute even by anything
מתיב רב שמעיה בר זעירא: the perforated pot -- if it grew by 1/200, forbidden: grew, yes; did not grow, no -- so the root is not forbidden
the mishna (Kilayim): one who passes a perforated pot through a vineyard -- if it grew by one two-hundredth, it is forbidden [so: grew, yes; did not grow, no]
Abaye: two verses -- 'ha-melea'a' and 'ha-zera': sown from the outset, at rooting; sown and brought in, only if it grew
Abaye: two verses are written -- 'lest the growth [ha-melea'a] be forfeited' and 'the seed [ha-zera]' (Deut 22:9)
Rav Mordechai in Reish Lakish's name: one-from-three -- if the argument reverts and comes by מה הצד, we refute by anything; if not, by leniency and stringency only, not by anything
Rav Adda bar Ahava: this says that kilei hakerem -- their root is forbidden, and they had a time of fitness before rooting
R' Shimon (via R' Shimon b. Yehuda): meat in milk is forbidden to eat
תניא נמי הכי: in R' Yosei HaGelili's locale they would eat fowl meat in milk -- so for him fowl is not forbidden even rabbinically
in R' Eliezer's locale they would cut wood to make charcoal to make iron
[what is between R' Yosei HaGelili and R' Akiva?] between them is a wild animal
if you wish, say: between them is fowl
Levi happened to come to the house of Yosef the fowler; they brought before him a peacock's head in milk, and he said nothing at all to them
Levi: it is R' Yehuda ben Beteira's place, and I said [to myself]: he expounded for them in accordance with R' Yosei HaGelili
the keva (congealed milk in the stomach) of a gentile['s animal] is forbidden
לכדשמואל: one 'kid' includes fat
לכדשמואל: one 'kid' includes a dead animal
לכדשמואל: one 'kid' includes a fetus
הני הא אפקינהו לכדשמואל -- the three 'kid's are spent on Shmuel's fat / carcass / fetus, so none is free to exclude a wild animal
הני הא אפקינהו לכדשמואל -- [the same kashya] none is free to exclude fowl
הני הא אפקינהו לכדשמואל -- [the same kashya] none is free to exclude a non-kosher animal
these [three mentions of 'kid'] -- they were already taken out for Shmuel's [derashot]
since a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition, the meat-and-milk ban falls on fat without a verse
since a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition, the meat-and-milk ban falls on a carcass without a verse
the 'kid' Shmuel spends on fat is free
the 'kid' Shmuel spends on a carcass is free
the 'kid' Shmuel spends on a fetus is free, since a fetus is a kid outright
קסבר רבי עקיבא איסור חל על איסור, חלב ומתה לא צריכי קרא, שליל גדי מעליא הוא -- איייתרו להו כולהו
קסבר רבי עקיבא איסור חל על איסור ... איייתרו להו כולהו -- [the same answer]
קסבר רבי עקיבא איסור חל על איסור ... איייתרו להו כולהו -- [the same answer]
R' Akiva holds: a prohibition takes effect upon a prohibition
